questions.question_text_en: What is the difference between reversible and irreversible reactions?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: In reversible reactions, the reaction goes to completion.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: In irreversible reactions, there is a mixture of products and reactants.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: In reversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: In irreversible reactions, there is equilibrium between reactants and products.

explanation.solution_text_en:
A reversible reaction can proceed in both directions and may establish dynamic equilibrium, where forward and 
reverse rates are equal.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en: Consider the reactions all given below are in gaseous state. For which of the following reactions is K p less than K c?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: N₂ O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 2H₂ ⇌ H₂ + I₂

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: N₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2NO

explanation.solution_text_en: Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. For 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃, Δn = 2 − 3 = −1, so Kp = Kc/(RT) and therefore Kp < Kc.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 5: Chemical Equilibrium

questions.question_text_en:
The heating curve shown below shows a substance in the solid, liquid and gas phase. Which segment represents only the 
liquid phase?

explanation.solution_text_en:
On a heating curve, sloped segments represent a single phase warming. Segment 3 lies between the melting and 
boiling plateaus, so it represents liquid only.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: The general formula for saturated monocarboxylic acids is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: RCOOH

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: RCOR

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: RCHO

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: ROR

explanation.solution_text_en: A saturated monocarboxylic acid contains one carboxyl group and is represented generally as RCOOH.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: What is enthalpy change? It is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure and volume

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the amount of heat absorbed in a reaction

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the amount of heat given out in a reaction

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the amount of heat given out or absorbed in a reaction at constant pressure

explanation.solution_text_en:
At constant pressure, the enthalpy change ΔH equals the heat absorbed or released by the system, which is option 
D.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 4: Energy Changes and Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: What is oxidation? Oxidation is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the addition of electron(s) to the oxidizing agent

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the reduction of the oxidation state of the oxidizing agent

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the addition of hydrogen to a substance and the removal of oxygen from a substance

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the loss of electrons by a species, accompanied by an increase in oxidation number

explanation.solution_text_en: Oxidation is loss of electrons and is accompanied by an increase in oxidation number.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: What is meant by preferential discharge, if a number of ions are present in a solution? It means that the one which requires

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: highest energy will be liberated first at a given electrode

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: highest energy will be liberated last at a given electrode

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: least energy will be liberated first at a given electrode

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: least energy will be liberated last at a given electrode

explanation.solution_text_en:
Preferential discharge means the ion/electrode process requiring the least energy (most favorable electrode potential 
under the conditions) occurs first.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a property of covalent compounds? Covalent compounds

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: is generally insoluble in water

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: is crystalline solids at room temperature

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: is non-volatile

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: has high melting and boiling points

explanation.solution_text_en:
Molecular covalent compounds are generally poor electrical conductors and many are insoluble in water; option A is 
the best general statement given.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a covalent molecule?

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CO3-

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: PCl3

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: NaCl

explanation.solution_text_en: PCl₃ is a neutral covalent molecular compound. NaCl is ionic, and the other listed species are polyatomic ions.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: What is the concentration of a solution? It is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the amount of solute needed to make a concentrated solution

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: number of moles of solute and number of moles of solvent

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the quantity of solute in a given quantity of solution

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the amount of solvent needed to dissolve a solute

explanation.solution_text_en:
Concentration expresses how much solute is present in a specified amount of solution (or sometimes solvent, 
depending on the concentration unit).
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en:
How many moles of C₁₂ H₂₂ O₁₁ (sucrose Molecular weight= 342.91 g/mol) is needed there to prepare 2.0 L of 0.3 M 
solution?

explanation.solution_text_en: Moles = M×V = 0.3 mol L⁻¹ × 2.0 L = 0.60 mol.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a correct Lewis structure for diazomethane (CH₂ N₂)?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Lewis Structure A [H₂C-N≡N]

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Lewis Structure B [H₂C=N=N]

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lewis Structure C [H₂C=N⁺=N⁻ (resonance form)]

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Lewis Structure D [HC≡N-NH]

explanation.solution_text_en:
The correct Lewis representation of diazomethane must satisfy valence electron count and formal 
charges/resonance; the supplied option C shows an acceptable H₂C=N⁺=N⁻ resonance form.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en:
At 75°C, the vapor pressure of pure water is 39 kPa. Which one of the vapor pressure of a solution obtained by dissolving 
34.2 g sucrose in 180 mL of water? (Assume that the density of water is 1.000 g/mL)

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 41.1 kPa

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 44.5 kPa

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 31.2 kPa

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 38.6 kPa

explanation.solution_text_en:
Moles H₂O ≈180/18=10.0; moles sucrose≈34.2/342≈0.10. Xwater≈10/10.1=0.990. Raoult’s law gives 
P≈0.990×39=38.6 kPa.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the colligative properties of electrolytes and non-electrolytes?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is very low compared to electrolytes

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The effect of non-electrolytes on colligative properties is the same as those of electrolytes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The effect of electrolytes on colligative properties is very high compared to non-electrolytes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The colligative properties of non-electrolytes are not considerably changed

explanation.solution_text_en:
Electrolytes produce more solute particles by dissociation, so they normally cause larger colligative effects than 
comparable non-electrolytes. Saying the effects are the same is false.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: For the reaction shown below, which of the following is a conjugate acid-base pair? HC₃ O⁻(aq) + H₂ O(l) ⇌ H₃ O⁺ + CO₃²⁻
questions.review_note: The attached archive has formula transcription errors. The intended conjugate pair is HCO₃⁻/CO₃²⁻.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: H₃ O⁺ and HCO₃⁻

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: HCO₄⁻ and CO₄²⁻

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: HCO₃⁻ and H₂ O

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: H₂ O and CO₂

explanation.solution_text_en:
The reaction is clearly intended to be HCO₃⁻ + H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + CO₃²⁻. HCO₃⁻/CO₃²⁻ differ by one proton and are a 
conjugate acid–base pair; the archive has formula transcription errors in option B.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: What is the purpose of synthetic cryolite in the extraction of aluminum by the Hall's process?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Cryolite increases the melting point of alumina.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Cryolite is used as a catalyst in the extraction of aluminum.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Cryolite increases the purity of the extracted aluminum.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Cryolite reduces the melting point of alumina.

explanation.solution_text_en:
Cryolite dissolves alumina and lowers the operating/melting temperature of the electrolyte in the Hall–Héroult 
process, reducing energy demand.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a chemical property of aluminum?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Aluminum is a good conductor of heat and electricity.

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Aluminum has a lower density than any other commercial metal.

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Aluminum liberates hydrogen gas from dilute acids like HCl and H₂ SO₄.

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Aluminum is a grey metal in color.

explanation.solution_text_en: Reaction with dilute acids to release H₂ is a chemical property; density, color and conductivity are physical properties.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: How is tanning carried out? In tanning the hides or skins are

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: treated with chromium salts

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: treated with dilute hydrochloric acid to remove the lime

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: soaked in water for several days

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: soaked in lime and water for several days

explanation.solution_text_en:
Tanning stabilizes hide proteins using tanning agents such as chromium(III) salts; option A describes the tanning 
step itself.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: How can a project of establishing an industry that consumes coal affect the environment?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Production of high level of lead in the atmosphere

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: By changing the pH of water

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Increment in concentration of nitric oxide

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Rise in global temperature

explanation.solution_text_en:
Coal combustion releases CO₂, a greenhouse gas, so large-scale coal use can contribute to global warming and 
rising global temperature.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 5: Introduction to Environmental Chemistry

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity SI unit?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Length

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Speed

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Force

explanation.solution_text_en: Length is an SI base quantity; pressure, speed and force are derived quantities.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following postulates of Dalton's atomic theory was modified by the modern atomic theory?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in chemical reactions

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Compounds are formed when atoms of more than one element combine

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Atoms are the smallest particles of all elements

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Atoms are indivisible and indestructible

explanation.solution_text_en:
Dalton’s idea that atoms are indivisible/indestructible was modified after discovery of subatomic particles and nuclear 
processes.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following includes all of the known atomic models?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Bohr Model, Rutherford Mechanical Model

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Thomson Model, Dalton's Atomic Model

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Bohr Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model, Dalton's Atomic Model

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Valence Bond Model, Quantum Mechanical Model, Thomson Model, Rutherford Model

explanation.solution_text_en:
Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford and Bohr are all historically recognized atomic models, so C is the complete list among 
the choices.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: The electron configuration of Cu (Z=29) is:
questions.review_note: No option gives the ground-state Cu configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: [Kr]4s² 3d⁹

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: [Ar]4s² 3d¹⁰

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: [Ar]4s² 3p⁸

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: [Ar]4s² 4d⁹

explanation.solution_text_en: The ground-state configuration of Cu is [Ar] 3d¹⁰4s¹. None of the supplied options matches that configuration.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: What does Mendeleev's Periodic Law state? Properties of elements are

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: periodic functions of their electron configurations

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: atomic radius

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: atomic numbers

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: atomic masses

explanation.solution_text_en:
Mendeleev’s periodic law related periodic properties to atomic mass, unlike the modern law which uses atomic 
number.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en:
What is the mole ratio of oxygen gas to carbon dioxide gas in the following reaction? C₃ H₈ (g) + 5O₂ (g) → 3CO₂ (g) + 4H₂ O 
(l)

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: 2 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: 7 mole oxygen gas to 5 mole carbon dioxide

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: 10 mole oxygen gas to 6 mole carbon dioxide

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: 5 mole oxygen gas to 3 mole carbon dioxide

explanation.solution_text_en: The balanced equation shows 5 mol O₂ for every 3 mol CO₂, so the ratio is 5:3.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 1: Chemical Reactions and Stoichiometry

questions.question_text_en: Among the following reactions, which one shows a coordinate covalent bond formation?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: H⁻ + ·Cl ^: → H-Cl

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: H⁻ + ·H → H:H

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: AlCl₃ + Cl⁻ → AlCl₄⁻ [coordinate bond]

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: BF₃ + :NH₃ → F₃B←NH₃ [Lewis adduct]

explanation.solution_text_en:
A coordinate bond forms when both bonding electrons are donated by one atom. The BF₃–NH₃ adduct shown in 
option D forms by donation of the NH₃ lone pair to electron-deficient B.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en:
Consider the following chemical equation for the combustion of ethane (C₂ H₆) in the presence of oxygen to produce carbon 
dioxide and water: C₂ H₆ (g) + 7O₂ (g) → 4CO₂ (g) + 6H₂ O (l) In this reaction:
questions.review_note:
The chemical equation in the source is unbalanced; the explanation uses the correctly balanced combustion 
equation.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Water is formed at a rate equal to 2/3 the rate of formation of CO₂

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CO₂ is formed twice as fast as ethane is consumed

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The rate of consumption of ethane is 7 times faster than the rate of consumption of oxygen

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The rate of formation of CO₂ equals the rate of formation of water

explanation.solution_text_en:
The printed ethane equation is not balanced; the balanced equation is 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. Thus CO₂ forms 
at twice the rate that ethane is consumed.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following factors DOES NOT affect the rate of a reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Temperature

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Enthalpy

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Surface area

explanation.solution_text_en:
Reaction rate depends on factors such as concentration, temperature, surface area and catalysts. Enthalpy change 
itself is not a standard kinetic control factor.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: How does a catalyst increase the rate of a reaction?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: By lowering the activation energy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: By changing the equilibrium constant

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: By forming an intermediate complex

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: By increasing the activation energy

explanation.solution_text_en:
A catalyst speeds a reaction by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy; it does not change the 
equilibrium constant.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements correctly describes Boyle's Law?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is proportional to the square root of the applied pressure

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the square root of the applied pressure

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is directly proportional to the applied pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at a given temperature is inversely proportional to the applied pressure

explanation.solution_text_en:
Boyle’s law states that, at constant temperature and amount of gas, volume is inversely proportional to pressure: V 
∝ 1/P.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter

questions.question_text_en: What are intermolecular forces? They are forces due to the attraction between

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: nuclei and electron pair

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: cations and delocalized electrons

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: molecules

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: cations and anions

explanation.solution_text_en: Intermolecular forces are attractions between separate molecules.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following belongs to chemical bonding theories?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Molecular orbital theory and kinetic-molecular theory

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Valence bond theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Kinetic-molecular theory and valence shell electron pair repulsion theory

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Valence bond theory and molecular orbital theory

explanation.solution_text_en:
Valence-bond theory and molecular-orbital theory are both fundamental theories of chemical bonding. VSEPR is 
mainly a molecular-shape model.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: In which of the following molecules is the central atom sp² hybridized?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: SO₂

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CO

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CO₂

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: N₂ O

explanation.solution_text_en:
SO₂ has three electron domains around sulfur (two bonding regions and one lone pair), giving an sp² electron-domain 
description in the conventional hybridization model.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: For a reaction: ½ A → the rate of disappearance of 'A' is related to the appearance of 'B' by the expression:

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: -Δ[A]/Δt = 1/2 Δ[B]/Δt

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Δ[A]/Δt = 1/4 Δ[B]/Δt

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: -Δ[A]/Δt = Δ[B]/Δt

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Δ[A]/Δt = 4Δ[B]/Δt

explanation.solution_text_en: For ½A → B, the stoichiometric rate relation is −(1/(1/2))d[A]/dt = d[B]/dt, hence −d[A]/dt = ½d[B]/dt.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: The half-life of a reaction is the time taken for the

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: rate constant to decrease by 50% of its initial value

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: complete conversion of a reactant into a product

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: reactant concentration to decrease by 50% of its initial value

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: rate constant to increase by 50% of its initial value

explanation.solution_text_en: Half-life is the time required for the reactant concentration to fall to one-half of its initial value.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 4: Chemical Kinetics

questions.question_text_en: For the conversion of 3.5 yards into meter using the factor label method, which of the following is the correct step?
questions.review_note: Every option uses the incorrect conversion 3.5 ft/yd. The correct factor is 3 ft/yd.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(1 in/2.54 cm)(1 m/100 cm)

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: (3.5 yards/1)(3.5 feet/1 yard)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1 m/100 cm)

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: (3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/1 foot)(2.54 cm/1 in)(1 m/100 cm)

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: (3.5 yards/1)(1 yard/3.5 feet)(12 in/1 foot)(1 in/2.54 cm)(1 m/100 cm)

explanation.solution_text_en:
Dimensional analysis requires 1 yd = 3 ft, not 3.5 ft. Option B has the correct orientation of factors but contains the 
wrong numerical conversion, so none is fully correct.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods

questions.question_text_en: In the scientific method, a predictive statement that can be tested experimentally is:

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: proof

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: hypothesis

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: truth

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: evidence

explanation.solution_text_en: A hypothesis is a tentative, testable predictive statement that can be examined experimentally.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 9 Chemistry — Unit 2: Measurements and Scientific Methods 
ESSLCE Chemistry 2014 E.C. | Questions, Answers & Explanations

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is NOT true about cathode rays? Cathode rays

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: contain particles, which are positively charged

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: are common constituents of all matter and their m/e is constant for all gases

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: contain particles, which are negatively charged

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: travel in straight lines from cathode to the anode

explanation.solution_text_en:
Cathode rays are streams of negatively charged electrons, so saying they contain positively charged particles is 
false.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is correct about the energy of a photon?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is directly related to the intensity of the light

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It is directly proportional to the wavelength of the light

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is directly proportional to the observed frequency of the light

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is inversely proportional to the observed frequency of the light

explanation.solution_text_en: Photon energy is E = hν, so it is directly proportional to frequency and inversely proportional to wavelength.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following explains the emission spectra of atoms consisting of a series of fine lines?
questions.review_note: Options C and D are nearly duplicate descriptions; D is selected as the clearest.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The energy of the atoms is continuous with discrete frequencies

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: An electron that revolves around the nucleus emits specific energy values in an atom

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: An electron can have specific transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wavelength

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: An electron undergoes a transition by energy changes corresponding to photon of specific wavelength

explanation.solution_text_en:
Line spectra arise because electrons can occupy discrete energy levels; transitions between specific levels 
emit/absorb photons of specific energies and wavelengths. D states this most directly, although C is worded very similarly.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 1: Atomic Structure and Periodic Properties of the Elements

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a polyprotic acid?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: HF

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: HNO₃

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: HCl

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: H₃ PO₄

explanation.solution_text_en: H₃PO₄ can donate more than one proton and is therefore polyprotic.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following does represent a general property of a base?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Soluble bases release hydronium ion in aqueous solution

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Aqueous solution of bases turns methyl orange to red

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Solutions of strong bases are good conductors of electricity

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Aqueous solution of bases turns blue litmus paper to red

explanation.solution_text_en: Strong bases dissociate extensively to produce mobile ions, so their aqueous solutions conduct electricity well.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: What are salts? Salts are

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ionic compounds that derive their cations from a base and their anions from an acid

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ionic compounds formed by partial replacement of ionizable hydrogen by metal cations

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ionic compounds formed by complete replacement of ionizable hydrogen by anions of the acid

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ionic compounds that result from the reaction between metal hydroxide and water

explanation.solution_text_en:
A salt is an ionic compound whose cation can be viewed as derived from a base and whose anion can be viewed as 
derived from an acid; A is the best general definition.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: The process in which a compound absorbs electrical energy and decomposes into its elements is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: hydrolysis

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: electropating

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: electrolysis

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: solvolysis

explanation.solution_text_en: Electrolysis uses electrical energy to drive a nonspontaneous decomposition/redox process.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is true about galvanic cells used in commercial lead storage batteries? In lead storage batteries,

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: half of the galvanic cells are connected in series

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the galvanic cells are made up of PbO₂ of anodes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: galvanic cells are connected in series

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: galvanic cells are connected in parallel

explanation.solution_text_en: A lead–acid battery uses multiple electrochemical cells connected in series to increase the total voltage.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 2: Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en:
The self-ionization of water can be expressed by the equation: H₂ O(l) + H₂ O(l)⇌ H₃ O⁺ (aq) + OH⁻ (aq) Which of the 
following is the correct expression of the ionic product of water?
questions.review_note: A and D are duplicate correct expressions for Kw.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: K w = [H₃ O⁺ ][OH⁻ ]

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: K w = [H₂ O][OH⁻ ]/[H₃ O⁺ ]

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: K w = [H₃ O⁺ ][HO⁻ ]

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: K w = [H₃ O⁺ ][OH⁻ ]

explanation.solution_text_en: For water autoionization, Kw = [H₃O⁺][OH⁻]. Options A and D are duplicates of the same correct expression.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: What is the effect of a common ion in an electrolytic solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It decreases the solubility of a solute

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It has no effect on the pH of a solution

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It suppresses the ionization of a weak acid and raises the pH

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It suppresses the ionization of a weak base and lowers the pOH

explanation.solution_text_en:
A common ion suppresses ionization of a weak electrolyte. For a weak acid/conjugate-base buffer, adding the 
conjugate base suppresses acid ionization and raises pH.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: Sodium carbonate is a basic salt because it is a salt of

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: a weak acid and a weak base and the cation of the weak base can be hydrolyzed

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a strong acid and a weak base and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a strong base and a weak acid and the anion of the weak acid can be hydrolyzed

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a strong base and a strong acid and the anion of the strong acid can be hydrolyzed

explanation.solution_text_en:
Na₂CO₃ comes from strong base NaOH and weak acid H₂CO₃; CO₃²⁻ hydrolyzes water to form OH⁻, making the 
solution basic.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is true for an acid-base titration?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: An acid-base titration is a method of quantitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: An acid-base titration is a method of qualitative analysis for determining the concentration of an acid or base

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Indicators catalyze an acid-base titration to show the inflection point of the titration curve

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Acid-base titrations cannot be carried out in the absence of indicators

explanation.solution_text_en:
Acid–base titration is a quantitative method used to determine an unknown acid/base concentration from 
stoichiometry and a measured equivalence/end point.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 1: Acid-Base Concepts

questions.question_text_en:
What is the change in internal energy (ΔE) for a reaction, in which the system absorbs 650 J of heat and 125 J of work is 
done on the system?

explanation.solution_text_en:
Using ΔE = q + w with the chemistry sign convention: q = +650 J and work done on the system w = +125 J, so ΔE = 
+775 J.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 4: Energy Changes and Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: Which statement describes the formation of a covalent bond? In covalent bond electrons are

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: shared between non-metallic atoms

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: transferred from non-metallic atoms to metallic atoms

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: shared between metallic atoms

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: transferred from metallic atoms to non-metallic atoms

explanation.solution_text_en: A covalent bond forms by sharing electron pairs, typically between nonmetal atoms.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: How do the elements of Group IIA form ions?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: By losing 2 electrons

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: By gaining 2 electrons

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: By gaining one electron

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: By losing one electron

explanation.solution_text_en: Group IIA atoms have two valence electrons and typically form 2+ ions by losing both.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals / Grade 11 bonding context

questions.question_text_en: How is hydrogen bonding formed? It is formed when a hydrogen atom is bonded to

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: highly electronegative elements, chlorine, oxygen and nitrogen

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, chlorine and oxygen

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: highly electronegative elements, fluorine, oxygen and phosphorus

explanation.solution_text_en: Strong hydrogen bonding occurs when H is covalently bonded to highly electronegative F, O or N.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 2: Chemical Bonding

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following types of energy change occurs from the combustion of carbon in oxygen?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: heat energy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: solar energy

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: light energy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: electrical energy

explanation.solution_text_en: Combustion is exothermic; the principal energy change is release of heat (often accompanied by light).
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 4: Energy Changes and Electrochemistry

questions.question_text_en: What is the molar volume of a gas?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 0°C and pressure,1 kPa), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure,1 kPa), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature, 0°C and pressure,1 atm), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The volume of a gas at STP (standard temperature 25°C and pressure,1 atm), which is equal to 22.4 L/mol

explanation.solution_text_en: At the traditional STP definition of 0°C and 1 atm, an ideal gas occupies about 22.4 L mol⁻¹.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following assumptions of the kinetic molecular theory of gases explains the high compressibility of gases?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Particles are always in random motion

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Different particles have different speeds

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The actual volume of gas molecules in negligible

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: There is no force of attraction between gas molecules

explanation.solution_text_en:
Gas particles occupy a very small fraction of the container volume, leaving large empty spaces that can be reduced 
by compression.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter

questions.question_text_en:
Consider a bottle containing water, water vapor and air in equilibrium. If the temperature decreases slightly, the amount of 
water vapor:

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: will decrease and the vapor pressure will increase

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: and vapor pressure will decrease

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: and vapor pressure will increase

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: will increase and the vapor pressure will decrease

explanation.solution_text_en:
Lowering temperature lowers equilibrium vapor pressure, so some vapor condenses and both vapor amount and 
vapor pressure decrease.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter

questions.question_text_en: Why do water droplets collect on the outside of a glass of water on a hot day?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: There will be a condensation of water vapor on the glass

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: There will be a sublimation of water vapor on the outside of a glass

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: There is heat exchange between the water in the glass and the surrounding

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Water from the glass starts to vaporize

explanation.solution_text_en: The cold glass cools nearby air below its dew point, so water vapor condenses into droplets on the outside surface.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 3: Physical States of Matter

questions.question_text_en: What are hydrocarbons? Compounds that contain

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: benzene rings only

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: benzene and its derivatives only

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: hydrogen and carbon with no benzene rings

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: hydrogen and carbon only

explanation.solution_text_en: Hydrocarbons are compounds made only of carbon and hydrogen.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 6: Hydrocarbons and Their Natural Sources

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statement is INCORRECT regarding the boiling points of alkanes?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Boiling points of straight chain alkanes is greater than that of branched chain alkanes

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The boiling point of cycloalkanes is higher than that of linear alkanes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Boiling points increases with stronger Van der Waals forces

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Surface area is the only factor that determines the boiling points of alkanes

explanation.solution_text_en:
Boiling point is influenced by molecular mass, shape/surface area and intermolecular dispersion forces; surface area 
is not the only factor.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals / Grade 11 bonding context

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about minerals and ores?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Minerals are the natural forms in which various metals exist

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ores are usually used to extract metals economically

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: All minerals are ores

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: All ores are minerals

explanation.solution_text_en:
Every ore is a mineral/mineral deposit suitable for economic extraction, but many minerals are not ores. Thus “all 
minerals are ores” is false.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: Why is CaCl₂ added to NaCl in a 1:1⁄2 ratio in the Down's cell for the manufacturing of sodium metal?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: CaCl₂ is used to lower the density of the mixture

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CaCl₂ is used as an electrolyte

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CaCl₂ is used as a catalyst

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: CaCl₂ is used to lower the melting temperature of NaCl

explanation.solution_text_en:
Adding CaCl₂ lowers the melting point of the electrolyte mixture in the Downs cell, allowing NaCl electrolysis at a 
lower operating temperature.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is NOT a major step in metallurgical processes?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Pretreatment

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Extracting the metal and refining

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Mining the ore

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Concentrating the ore

explanation.solution_text_en:
Mining obtains the ore; the main metallurgical processing stages after mining are concentration/pretreatment, 
extraction and refining. Thus “mining the ore” is not a metallurgical processing step in the intended classification.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 3: Industrial Chemistry / Grade 10 Unit 5: Metals and Nonmetals

questions.question_text_en: Which monomers are used for the synthesis of Teflon?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Styrene and Phenol

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Tetrafluoroethylene

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Isoprene

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Propylene

explanation.solution_text_en: Teflon (PTFE) is an addition polymer made from tetrafluoroethylene, CF₂=CF₂.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 12 Chemistry — Unit 4: Polymers

questions.question_text_en: What is the IUPAC name of an ester having the molecular formula C₄H₉O₂?
questions.review_note: The stated molecular formula C₄H₉O₂ is inconsistent with a neutral saturated ester; no listed name matches it.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Ethyl butyrate

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Pentyl butyrate

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ethyl butanoate

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Methyl butyrate

explanation.solution_text_en:
A neutral saturated monocarboxylic ester has general formula C�H₂�O₂. C₄H₉O₂ does not match such a neutral 
ester, and none of the listed names has that formula.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: What is the formula of pentanoic acid?
questions.review_note: A and D duplicate the same correct formula.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: CH₃(CH₂)₃COOH

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: CH₃(CH₂)₄COOH

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: CH₃(CH₂)₂COOH

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: CH₃(CH₂)₃COOH

explanation.solution_text_en: Pentanoic acid has five total carbon atoms: CH₃(CH₂)₃COOH. Options A and D duplicate this same correct formula.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: What is the rate of dissolution? It is

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the rate at which a solid dissociates

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the speed at which a solid sublimes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the rate at which a solid turns to liquid

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the speed at which a solid substrate goes into solution

explanation.solution_text_en: Rate of dissolution is how quickly a solute enters solution from the solid phase.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correctly stated regarding solubility as an equilibrium process?
questions.review_note:
A and D are both chemically true; A is selected because the question emphasizes solubility as an equilibrium 
process.

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Supersaturated solution is a solution that contains more than the equilibrium amount of dissolved solute

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Supersaturated solution is more stable than saturated solution

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Unsaturated solution is a solution that is in equilibrium with respect to a given dissolved substance

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Unsaturated solution is a solution in which more of the solute can be dissolved

explanation.solution_text_en:
A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than the equilibrium solubility at that condition. D is also a 
true description of an unsaturated solution, so the item is not strictly unique; A is the statement tied most directly to equilibrium 
amount.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 10 Chemistry — Unit 2: Solutions

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following carboxylic acids is a solid substance at room temperature?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Nonanoic acid

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Decanoic acid

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Heptanoic acid

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Octanoic acid

explanation.solution_text_en:
Decanoic acid has a melting point around room temperature and is solid under typical room conditions, whereas the 
shorter acids listed are liquids at ordinary room temperature.
explanation.key_concept: Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following represents the structure of a disaccharide?

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Monosaccharide ring structure

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Branched polysaccharide unit

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Polysaccharide chain segment

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Disaccharide with glycosidic linkage

explanation.solution_text_en:
A disaccharide contains two monosaccharide rings joined by a glycosidic linkage; option D shows that structural 
feature.
explanation.key_concept:
Curriculum link: Grade 11 Chemistry — Unit 6: Some Important Oxygen-containing Organic Compounds
